name: Dr Agarwal's Eye Hospital Ltd (DAEHL)
tagline: High-quality regional eye-care operator, but now effectively a merger-arbitrage proxy on parent Dr Agarwal's Health Care at a fixed swap ratio
business_overview: DAEHL is the BSE-listed (526783) regional eye-hospital operator of the Dr Agarwal's group, concentrated largely in Tamil Nadu / South India. Its promoter is the pan-India parent Dr Agarwal's Health Care Ltd (DAHL), which IPO'd in Jan-Feb 2025. In Aug 2025 the group announced a merger of DAEHL into DAHL at a swap ratio of 23 DAHL shares for every 2 DAEHL shares. As of mid-2026 the merger is still pending SEBI and then NCLT approval, with a fresh internal team on it and completion guided (loosely) to Q3/Q4 FY27 and widely expected to slip.
fundamentals_table: ~17.7% revenue CAGR; same-store sales growth ~13% (roughly half value, half volume) per latest concall
Modest at the listed-entity level; group (DAHL) balance sheet carries more leverage
Rs 4,600 - 6,060 (was at a 52-week low around 20 Aug 2026)
fundamentals_narrative: On its own numbers DAEHL is a genuinely high-quality asset: ROCE ~42%, ROE ~36%, mid-to-high-teens revenue growth and ~13% same-store sales growth, in a structurally growing single-speciality (eye care / cataract / refractive) segment with an ageing-population and premiumisation tailwind. It is also cheaper than its own parent on EV/EBITDA despite better return ratios and growth — the classic 'listed regional subsidiary' discount. The catch is that the fixed 2:23 merger swap ratio caps DAEHL holders' outcome to whatever the parent does, minus the ~8-11% arbitrage/dilution the community has debated back and forth. Promoter has deliberately grown the regional franchise slower than the pan-India parent, which is itself a minority-shareholder-friendliness question.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Community noted the stock hit a 52-week low around 20 Aug 2026 despite no fundamental deterioration, likely merger-timeline fatigue plus rotation into the parent's IPO stock.
sentiment_summary: First-time read of the full thread (44 posts, Sep 2023 - Aug 2026, single batch, no escalation). Early posts are basic business appreciation; from early 2025 the thread is dominated by the parent's IPO (shareholder-quota buying spiked DAEHL's shareholder count from ~4,500 to ~15,000 in one quarter) and then, from Aug 2025, entirely by the merger swap ratio. Sustained disagreement between Sidharth_Chandraseka (2:23 is a poor deal for DAEHL holders given superior fundamentals; the regional-only growth cap is 'lack of intention, not opportunity') and varvp14 / Omkar_Ranjan (fair, you effectively get the larger pan-India parent ~9-20% cheaper, plus operating synergies). Most recent substantive post (Manan_Nandu, May 2026): spoke to IR, merger team reshuffled, SEBI approval still pending, NCLT after that, timeline likely to slip past guidance.
community_signal: Trusted-roster user shyamutty posted once (post #11, 2024, 0 love) — not a conviction call. vikasbargale (trusted-roster, post #31, 3 love) gave only a factual explanation of the regional-vs-pan-India valuation gap. No trusted-roster user made a directional high-conviction call in this thread. Highest-loved posts are Surender's opening business write-up (14) and Ashar_Mann's early note (15), both pre-merger.
bse_notes: Merger scheme (2 DAEHL : 23 DAHL) filed with exchanges Aug 2025; awaiting SEBI then NCLT sanction as of the latest thread posts (May 2026).

value_chain.position: Regional (Tamil Nadu / South) eye-care hospital chain within the Dr Agarwal's group; being absorbed into the pan-India parent Dr Agarwal's Health Care Ltd
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Surgeon density / trained ophthalmologist capacity and brand trust in the catchment; premium (refractive, cataract IOL mix) pricing power
value_chain.note: Eye-care single-speciality has attractive unit economics (high ROCE, short payback per centre, day-care surgical model). DAEHL captures the segment cleanly but its equity value is now mechanically pinned to the parent via the swap ratio; the standalone quality is the reason the merger terms are contested, not a reason to own DAEHL over DAHL.

bull_case: Genuinely high-quality economics: ROCE ~42%, ROE ~36%, ~17% revenue CAGR, ~13% same-store growth in a structurally growing single-speciality segment
Trades at ~19x EV/EBITDA vs parent's ~28x with better return ratios — a real quality-at-a-discount gap that the merger is meant to close
Merger into the pan-India parent gives exposure to a much larger growth runway plus operating synergies; effectively a cheaper entry into DAHL
Eye-care demand tailwind (ageing population, rising cataract volumes, premium IOL / refractive mix) is durable
bear_case: Fixed 2:23 swap ratio caps the outcome to the parent's trajectory; the standalone quality gap does not accrue to DAEHL holders
Merger has been pending for a year, team was reshuffled, SEBI and NCLT approvals still outstanding — dead-money risk until it closes
Promoter deliberately grew the regional entity slower than the parent, a minority-friendliness flag
At ~Rs 2,400 Cr and mid-teens growth this is not a 10x-in-2-3-years or 100x-in-10-years candidate on any realistic path; it is a compounder/arbitrage, not a multibagger setup
Post-merger the position simply becomes DAHL, which trades at a full ~28x EV/EBITDA large-cap multiple
verdict_headline: Excellent little business, but the fixed merger swap turns it into an arbitrage on the parent — no multibagger math here
verdict_reasoning: Standalone fundamentals (42% ROCE, 36% ROE, ~13-17% growth) are strong and the segment tailwind is real, but a ~Rs 2,400 Cr mid-teens compounder being merged into a ~Rs 14,000 Cr parent at a fixed ratio cannot deliver 10x in 2-3 years or 100x in 10 years
Upside is bounded by the parent's growth minus the 8-11% arbitrage/dilution the community itself keeps arriving at; the interesting quality gap does not transfer to DAEHL shareholders
No red flag; no trusted-roster high-conviction call in the thread; conviction Medium on a good-but-capped situation
Theme match (P2): Single-speciality hospitals & diagnostics — surfaced via recency discovery on the DAEHL thread
Re-check trigger is the merger closing (SEBI/NCLT); until then it is a merger-timeline holding, not a fresh idea
disclaimer: Community-sourced research notes for a personal screen. Not investment advice. Figures are as-reported by third-party aggregators and forum posts and were not independently audited.

four_box.note: value_chain: surgeon density+brand trust give premium pricing power (moat=yes); equity mechanically pinned to parent's swap ratio caps tam.

track_record.note: FY19-FY26 screener. Both revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% in the same FY: FY19, FY22, FY23, FY24, FY25, FY26 (ROCE 17-34%, growth 11-44%). Missed only FY20 (rev +4%) and FY21 (COVID, rev -20%). ROCE has settled at a steady 17-20% since FY22 as the centre network scaled.

quality_metrics.note: FY26 ROCE 17% / ROE 25%, OPM ~31%. Borrowings Rs 326 Cr vs EBITDA ~Rs 146 Cr FY26 (~2.2x, partly Ind AS 116 hospital lease liabilities). CFO Rs 145 Cr FY26. Day-care surgical eye-care model has short payback per centre and ROCE held ~17-20% right through the roll-out - capex_efficiency productive. Note: equity value is now mechanically pinned to parent DAHL via the fixed 2:23 merger swap.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: equity value is mechanically pinned to parent DAHL via the fixed 2 DAEHL : 23 DAHL swap; standalone ~19x EV/EBITDA vs the parent's ~28x on ~14-16% same-store + centre-roll-out growth implies a mid-teens EPS CAGR, but the realised outcome is whatever DAHL does minus the ~8-11% arbitrage/dilution the thread keeps arriving at
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: revenue ~Rs 650-720 Cr; post-merger the position simply becomes DAHL at ~28x EV/EBITDA
market_expectation.gap_basis: after the announced 2:23 merger (pending SEBI then NCLT, likely to slip past FY27) DAEHL is a merger-arbitrage proxy on the parent. Standalone ROCE ~17% / ROE ~25% and ~19x EV/EBITDA are attractive vs the parent's ~28x, but that discount is what the swap is meant to close, not upside for DAEHL holders.
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view
